nexusClaim.associationBasis: Rosacea associates with depression at nationwide-cohort and general-population level, with a severity gradient: the Danish nationwide register study linking 4,632,341 adults between 1997 and 2011 identified 30,725 patients with mild rosacea and 24,712 with moderate-to-severe rosacea and found both groups at increased risk of depression, with crude and adjusted incidence rate ratios of 1.89 (95 percent CI 1.82-1.96) for mild and 2.04 (95 percent CI 1.96-2.12) for moderate-to-severe disease, described as a disease severity-dependent increased risk (PMID 26954304); the 2026 large-scale retrospective matched cohort of more than 116 million patients including 335,314 with rosacea reports that at five years post-diagnosis rosacea patients had a significantly increased risk of depression (HR 1.488, 95 percent CI 1.451-1.527) and anxiety (HR 1.664), that observed risks continued to increase over time, and that the authors note the potential for miscoding and the absence of causal inference and severity ratings as limitations (PMID 41232679); and the Taiwanese nationwide database study of 7,881 patients with rosacea and 31,524 age- and sex-matched controls from 2000 to 2013 found an adjusted hazard ratio of 2.761 (95 percent CI 2.650-2.877, P<0.001) for psychiatric disorders overall after adjusting for age, sex, comorbidity, and region, with the highest adjusted hazard ratios for phobic disorder at 7.841 and obsessive-compulsive disorder at 6.389, and no rosacea subtype, severity, or laboratory data available in that database (PMID 30466187); recorded as documented association only with the anchor limits carried openly - all three anchors are register or claims-database designs that code diagnoses rather than apply structured instruments, one reports a composite psychiatric endpoint rather than depression specifically, and the same anchors report comorbid psychiatric conditions without establishing which preceded which.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation of depressive disorder is established for any individual: the located anchors are three register or claims cohorts using coded diagnoses rather than validated instruments, the two largest are conditioned on a diagnosed rosacea population that is itself selected by healthcare-seeking and coding practice, the third uses a composite psychiatric endpoint whose depression component is not separately reported, rosacea-related stigma and reduced quality of life are described as mediators rather than confounders and remain entangled with the skin disease, and the same population is exposed to the antidepressants that treat depression which can themselves act on flushing; individual claims require dated structured depression assessment or a documented depressive-disorder diagnosis with treatment record, dated rosacea diagnosis with severity, and exclusion of adjustment disorder, bipolar disorder, thyroid disease, and antidepressant-related flushing.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Facial erythema, visible telangiectasia, papules, and burning - a chronic disfiguring facial dermatosis repeatedly described in the anchors as affecting self-esteem and quality of life - are hypothesized to produce social avoidance, stigmatisation, and reduced self-image whose downstream effect is depressive illness, the route the survey anchor describes when it reports a path model in which anxiety and depressive symptoms are linked to somatic symptoms indirectly, mediated through quality of life and stigmatisation (PMID 24088195); whether the skin disease produced any individual's depression remains hypothesized until the psychiatric and dermatological courses are dated independently.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at triple-nationwide-cohort class following the mood-edge convention (the registered depressive-disorder convention with edges from 88 primaries, and the restless-leg-syndrome, insomnia, phantom-limb-pain, and postherpetic-neuralgia mood edges in batches 78, 71, and 73): the Danish register anchor is the only located design that separates rosacea by severity and demonstrates a severity-dependent gradient, 1.89 for mild and 2.04 for moderate-to-severe (PMID 26954304), the 116-million-patient matched cohort supplies the largest absolute sample and reports risks that increased over five years (PMID 41232679), and the Taiwanese database anchor supplies an independent national replication with a markedly higher overall psychiatric hazard ratio (PMID 30466187); because all three anchors use coded diagnoses, the third uses a composite psychiatric endpoint, and the authors of the largest explicitly disclaim causal inference, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only with those limits stated and routes individual claims through dated structured psychiatric assessment with adjustment disorder and bipolar disorder excluded.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: All three anchors use register or claims-coded diagnoses rather than validated depression instruments, and none reports a structured depression-specific endpoint except through composite psychiatric coding; the two largest anchors condition on a diagnosed rosacea population selected by healthcare-seeking and coding behaviour, so ascertainment bias cannot be excluded; the largest anchor explicitly disclaims causal inference and notes possible miscoding and absent severity ratings; the third anchor reports a composite psychiatric hazard ratio of 2.761 without a separately reported depression component; no located anchor establishes temporal ordering, since rosacea patients treated with antidepressants can develop flushing from the medication itself.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Adjustment disorder or distress proportionate to a chronic visible facial condition rather than major depressive disorder
Bipolar disorder, for which the located claim-based literature shows elevated hazard and which is excluded by the composite endpoint of one anchor
Concomitant thyroid disease, the registered thyroid-condition depression window ownable separately
Antidepressant-induced flushing or sweating mimicking or aggravating rosacea, a treatment-mediated route running opposite to the proposed direction

evidenceGaps: All three anchors use register or claims-coded diagnoses rather than validated depression instruments, and none reports a structured depression-specific endpoint except through composite psychiatric coding; the two largest anchors condition on a diagnosed rosacea population selected by healthcare-seeking and coding behaviour, so ascertainment bias cannot be excluded; the largest anchor explicitly disclaims causal inference and notes possible miscoding and absent severity ratings; the third anchor reports a composite psychiatric hazard ratio of 2.761 without a separately reported depression component; no located anchor establishes temporal ordering, since rosacea patients treated with antidepressants can develop flushing from the medication itself.
suggestions.rationale: Authoring registers this edge as the strongest of the four rosacea edges because two very large national cohorts and one independent national replication quantify the association with a severity gradient and time course; the conservative framing names the coded-diagnosis limitation, the ascertainment bias inherent in claims conditioning, the composite endpoint in the third anchor, the authors' own causal disclaimer, and the antidepressant-flushing counter-route, so the association is visible while direction remains unasserted.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Rosacea associates with anxiety symptoms and anxiety disorders at general-population, survey, and cross-country comparison level: the Northern Finland Birth Cohort 1966 clinical whole-body examination at 46-year follow-up of 1,932 subjects found rosacea in 15.1 percent (292 subjects) and, after adjustment for confounders, a 1.6-fold risk of psychiatric symptoms on the Hopkins Symptom Checklist-25 (OR 1.55, 95 percent CI 1.02-2.32), with the depression subscale separately at OR 1.56 (95 percent CI 1.10-2.18) (PMID 38008081); the 2014 survey of 168 people with rosacea reports a HADS anxiety score of 7.2 plus or minus 4.60 and a HADS depression score of 5.1 plus or minus 4.09 alongside a Dermatology Life Quality Index of 4.05 plus or minus 4.67 and a rejection scale score of 2.61 plus or minus 3.37, with path analysis suggesting that symptoms of anxiety and depression are linked with somatic symptoms indirectly, mediated through quality of life and stigmatisation, and that men are more negatively affected (PMID 24088195); and the 2025 case-control analysis of 200 Chinese patients with rosacea and 200 healthy participants reports higher Patient Health Questionnaire-9 scores for depression than controls and higher Dermatology Life Quality Index scores with 40.5 percent of the rosacea group showing a large and 45.5 percent an extremely large effect, while finding no significant links with dry eye syndrome, migraine, hypertension, or several other comorbidities, and establishing that no significance was found for a broad set of candidate associations (PMID 40741710); recorded as documented association only with the instrument and scale limits carried openly - the birth-cohort anchor is the only located design with a population denominator and uses a screening checklist rather than a structured anxiety diagnosis, the survey anchor has no control group, and the third anchor is a single-centre case-control design whose positive findings concern depression and quality of life rather than an anxiety instrument.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation of anxiety disorder is established for any individual: the only anchor with a population denominator is a 46-year single-point examination using a 25-item screening checklist whose confidence interval is wide, the survey anchor has no control group so its HADS anxiety mean cannot be compared to a norm, the third anchor reports depression and quality-of-life instruments rather than an anxiety measure, the same 200-patient anchor is a material counterweight in reporting that its rosacea group showed no significant association with several candidate comorbidities, and general anxiety is plausibly both a consequence of facial disfigurement and a pre-existing trait that shapes healthcare-seeking; individual claims require dated structured anxiety assessment or a documented anxiety-disorder diagnosis, dated rosacea diagnosis with severity, and exclusion of social anxiety arising from the facial condition itself, illness anxiety, and pre-existing generalised anxiety.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Visible and burning facial inflammation perceived by others, combined with the survey-anchored rejection-scale experience of being visibly stared at, is hypothesized to produce anticipatory social threat and avoidance that presents as generalised anxiety, the route the survey anchor's path model describes when anxiety and depressive symptoms reach somatic symptoms indirectly through quality of life and stigmatisation rather than directly; whether the skin disease produced any individual's anxiety disorder remains hypothesized until the anxiety course and the dermatological course are dated independently.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at population-clinical-examination, cross-sectional-survey, and single-centre-case-control class following the mood-edge convention established by the 88 registered depressive-disorder edges and their sibling anxiety edges: the birth-cohort anchor is the strongest located design because it applies dermatologist-performed examination rather than self-report to define rosacea and adjusts for confounders, with the depression subscale analysed separately (PMID 38008081), the survey anchor supplies the validated anxiety instrument with the quality-of-life and rejection scales and the mediation model (PMID 24088195), and the Chinese case-control anchor supplies an independent design in a different population with a quality-of-life effect distribution (PMID 40741710); because the population anchor uses a screening checklist with a wide confidence interval, the survey anchor has no comparator group, and the third anchor reports depression rather than anxiety instruments, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only with those instrument limits stated and the third anchor's own null findings carried openly as counterweight.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: The only anchor with a population denominator uses the Hopkins Symptom Checklist-25, a screening instrument whose 95 percent CI of 1.02-2.32 is wide, and applies a single-point 46-year examination rather than incident ascertainment; the survey anchor has no control group, so its HADS anxiety mean of 7.2 has no comparator in the same study; the third anchor reports depression and quality-of-life instruments rather than any anxiety measure and is therefore registered for the quality-of-life and depression context rather than as an anxiety anchor; that same third anchor reports no significant association with several candidate comorbidities, an explicit counterweight carried here; no located anchor uses a structured anxiety-disorder diagnostic interview.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Pre-existing generalised anxiety disorder as a trait shaping both healthcare-seeking and rosacea severity
Social anxiety or body-dysmorphic disorder arising specifically from the visible facial condition
Illness anxiety about the skin diagnosis itself, for which the catalog carries a distinct illness-anxiety-disorder identity
Concomitant depression, which the population anchor's depression-subscale result shows tracks alongside the anxiety result

evidenceGaps: The only anchor with a population denominator uses the Hopkins Symptom Checklist-25, a screening instrument whose 95 percent CI of 1.02-2.32 is wide, and applies a single-point 46-year examination rather than incident ascertainment; the survey anchor has no control group, so its HADS anxiety mean of 7.2 has no comparator in the same study; the third anchor reports depression and quality-of-life instruments rather than any anxiety measure and is therefore registered for the quality-of-life and depression context rather than as an anxiety anchor; that same third anchor reports no significant association with several candidate comorbidities, an explicit counterweight carried here; no located anchor uses a structured anxiety-disorder diagnostic interview.
suggestions.rationale: Authoring registers this edge because the population anchor applies dermatologist-performed examination with confounder adjustment, the survey anchor supplies validated anxiety and quality-of-life instruments with an explicit mediation model, and a third independent design adds a different population; the conservative framing names the screening-instrument limitation, the missing comparator group, the absence of an anxiety measure in the third anchor, and that anchor's own null findings, so the association is visible while a structured anxiety diagnosis remains the requirement for any individual claim.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Ocular involvement is a well-characterised manifestation of rosacea, with meibomian gland dysfunction and blepharoconjunctivitis the most common ocular findings and dry eye quantified in large case-control designs: the multi-institutional Korean case-control study of 12,936 rosacea patients and an equal number of sex- and age-matched controls over a 12-year period found notable associations with blepharitis (adjusted odds ratio 3.44, 95 percent CI 2.71-4.36, P<0.001), conjunctivitis (aOR 1.65, 95 percent CI 1.50-1.82, P<0.001), glaucoma (aOR 1.93, 95 percent CI 1.70-2.20, P<0.001), dry eye syndrome (aOR 1.89, 95 percent CI 1.70-2.09, P<0.001), and chalazion (aOR 3.26, 95 percent CI 1.41-7.57, P=0.006), concluding ocular comorbidities are more prevalent among rosacea patients and that clinicians should proactively check ocular symptoms and co-manage with ophthalmology (PMID 34209731); the 2021 clinical review states that the most common ocular features are chronic blepharoconjunctivitis with eyelid-margin inflammation and meibomian gland dysfunction, that corneal complications include vascularisation, ulceration, scarring and rarely perforation, and that diagnosis is largely based on clinical signs but is often delayed in the absence of cutaneous changes, particularly in children (PMID 33403718); and the 2003 comparison of 176 patients diagnosed with acne rosacea by ophthalmology and by dermatology found meibomian gland dysfunction significantly more frequent in the ophthalmology-diagnosed group, and concludes that the major and most easily observable ocular problems in rosacea patients presenting to either service are lid disease-related manifestations (PMID 12658088); recorded as documented association only with the ascertainment limits carried openly - the case-control anchor is derived from a single national dermatology cohort and the ophthalmology comparison anchor measures the difference between referral pathways rather than the prevalence of ocular disease in rosacea, so its positive findings reflect where patients were first seen.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation of dry eye syndrome is established for any individual: the located case-control anchor derives from a dermatology service cohort so its ocular diagnoses are those recorded in dermatology charts, the ophthalmology anchor's between-service differences are referral-ascertainment effects rather than disease severity, the 2025 Chinese case-control anchor in the same publication family reports no significant association between rosacea and dry eye syndrome, and the direction is genuinely bidirectional since ocular rosacea is frequently the presenting sign when cutaneous changes are absent, particularly in children; individual claims require dated dry-eye diagnosis with objective tear-film or meibomian-gland assessment, dated rosacea diagnosis including ocular subtype, and exclusion of contact-lens use, ocular medications, Sjögren-type dryness, and prior ocular surgery.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Inflammatory and vascular dysregulation shared between facial skin and ocular surface, with lid-margin inflammation and meibomian gland dysfunction producing a deficient and unstable tear film - the mechanism the review anchor describes when it names chronic blepharoconjunctivitis with meibomian gland dysfunction as the most common ocular feature - so that ocular-surface dryness follows the lid disease, but whether the facial condition produced any individual's dry eye remains hypothesized and the located literature equally supports ocular-first presentation.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at multi-institutional-case-control, clinical-review, and referral-cohort-comparison class following the ocular-manifestation convention (the registered sjogren-s-syndrome and ichthyosis to dry-eye-syndrome edges, and the registered uveitis to glaucoma and myopia to glaucoma edges owning the anterior-segment and intraocular-pressure routes with sources left untouched per ME-29): the case-control anchor is the strongest located quantitative design and reports dry eye syndrome at an adjusted odds ratio of 1.89 alongside higher odds for blepharitis at 3.44 and chalazion at 3.26 (PMID 34209731), the clinical-review anchor supplies the mechanism and the ocular-first presentation problem (PMID 33403718), and the referral-comparison anchor supplies the independent observation that lid disease is the dominant and most observable ocular problem, and that its apparent frequency depends on which service makes the diagnosis (PMID 12658088); because the case-control anchor is drawn from dermatology-coded records, the referral anchor's difference is an ascertainment effect, and the same-publication null from the 2025 Chinese cohort is carried openly, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only with those limits stated.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: The case-control anchor derives its ocular diagnoses from dermatology service records, so ocular ascertainment is incomplete for patients not referred to ophthalmology; the referral-comparison anchor measures the difference between which service made the diagnosis, not the prevalence or severity of ocular disease, and its positive findings are consistent with referral behaviour alone; a separate 2025 Chinese case-control analysis of 200 rosacea patients found no significant association with dry eye syndrome, an explicit counterweight carried here; the clinical-review anchor notes that ocular diagnosis is often delayed when cutaneous changes are absent, particularly in children, so ocular-first presentations are systematically under-represented in cutaneous cohorts; the case-control anchor's glaucoma association overlaps a route the registered uveitis and myopia windows already own.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Sjögren-type or autoimmune dry eye, the registered sjogren-s-syndrome to dry-eye-syndrome window, which supplies the same target identity by a different route
Contact-lens wear, ocular topical medications, or prior ocular surgery producing iatrogenic dryness
Anterior-chamber inflammation from uveitis, the registered uveitis window, which can present with a dry eye from a different mechanism
Screen-time, low-humidity environment, and blink-rate reduction as independent contributors to evaporative dry eye

evidenceGaps: The case-control anchor derives its ocular diagnoses from dermatology service records, so ocular ascertainment is incomplete for patients not referred to ophthalmology; the referral-comparison anchor measures the difference between which service made the diagnosis, not the prevalence or severity of ocular disease, and its positive findings are consistent with referral behaviour alone; a separate 2025 Chinese case-control analysis of 200 rosacea patients found no significant association with dry eye syndrome, an explicit counterweight carried here; the clinical-review anchor notes that ocular diagnosis is often delayed when cutaneous changes are absent, particularly in children, so ocular-first presentations are systematically under-represented in cutaneous cohorts; the case-control anchor's glaucoma association overlaps a route the registered uveitis and myopia windows already own.
suggestions.rationale: Authoring registers this edge because ocular involvement is the condition's most frequently documented extra-cutaneous feature, a large case-control quantifies it, and a review supplies the mechanism; the conservative framing states the dermatology-record ascertainment limit, the referral-behaviour explanation for the comparison anchor's positive findings, the same-publication null, and the ocular-first presentation problem, so the association is visible while neither direction is asserted.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Rosacea and migraine overlap substantially across a meta-analysis, a cross-sectional phenotyping study, and a clinical comparison: the 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis of 11 observational studies including 112,994 rosacea patients and 4,402,330 non-rosacea participants found migraine prevalence of 25 percent in rosacea patients (95 percent CI 0.15 to 0.35, P<0.001, I-squared 99 percent) and nearly twice the odds of migraine versus controls (OR 1.93, 95 percent CI 1.42 to 2.64, P<0.001, I-squared 98 percent, 95 percent prediction interval 0.67 to 5.53), identifying erythrotelangiectatic subtype, female gender, age, and severity as potential contributing factors while concluding that substantial heterogeneity, including a prediction interval spanning the null, limits definitive conclusions (PMID 40899443); the 2022 cross-sectional study of 604 patients phenotyped by face-to-face interview with clinical examination found a prevalence of migraine of 54 percent in patients with rosacea and a prevalence of rosacea of 65 percent in patients with migraine, with concomitant migraine significantly associated with flushing (OR 2.6, 95 percent CI 1.4-4.7, P=0.002), ocular symptoms (OR 2.4, 95 percent CI 1.5-3.9, P<0.001), and burning (OR 2.1, 95 percent CI 1.3-3.4, P=0.002), while papules and pustules were inversely related (OR 0.5, 95 percent CI 0.3-0.8, P=0.006) (PMID 36341245); and the 2026 study of 150 rosacea patients and matched controls found headaches and migraine both more prevalent in rosacea patients than in controls (P<0.0001 and P=0.0006 respectively), with ocular symptoms present in 51.3 percent and more frequent in those with migraine (P=0.03) (PMID 42390920); recorded as documented association only with the heterogeneity and direction limits carried openly - the meta-analysis' prediction interval of 0.67 to 5.53 includes the null, the cross-sectional anchor reports prevalence in both directions and so establishes overlap rather than sequence, and the third anchor is a 150-patient single-centre comparison.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation of migraine is established for any individual: the meta-analysis reports I-squared of 99 percent for prevalence and 98 percent for the pooled odds ratio with a 95 percent prediction interval of 0.67 to 5.53 that includes the null, so the pooled estimate does not hold in every population, the cross-sectional anchor conditions on one or the other diagnosis and therefore cannot establish which preceded, its inverse finding for papules and pustules indicates the association is phenotype-specific rather than general, and a trigeminal neuropeptide pathway plausibly contributes to both conditions; individual claims require dated ICHD-3 migraine diagnosis with a headache diary, dated rosacea diagnosis with subtype, and exclusion of medication-over-use headache, prior migraine predating the skin diagnosis, and concurrent systemic inflammatory disease.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Facial neuropeptide release and vasomotor reactivity in rosacea - the pathway the located literature ties to elevated plasma calcitonin gene-related peptide and to anti-CGRP development of acne and rosacea - plausibly lowers the headache threshold in the trigeminovascular system so that headache-prone individuals experience migraine more often, the route the cross-sectional anchor supports through its flushing and burning associations and the meta-analysis through its erythrotelangiectatic subtype finding, but whether the skin condition produced any individual's migraine remains hypothesized and the shared-trigeminal-substrate reading is equally consistent with the located data.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at meta-analysis, cross-sectional-phenotyping, and clinical-comparison class following the comorbidity-magnitude convention (the registered ocd, ptsd, abdominal-migraine, alice-in-wonderland-syndrome, cyclic-vomiting-syndrome, and occipital-neuralgia to migraine-headaches edges, and this batch's rhinitis-vasomotor to migraine-headaches edge which uses an entirely disjoint source set per ME-29): the meta-analysis anchor is the only located synthesis and quantifies nearly doubled odds with the largest sample base (PMID 40899443), the cross-sectional anchor is the only located design with face-to-face clinical phenotyping of both conditions and identifies which cutaneous features carry the association (PMID 36341245), and the clinical-comparison anchor adds an independent population with concurrent ocular-symptom data (PMID 42390920); because the meta-analysis' prediction interval spans the null, the cross-sectional anchor reports prevalence in both directions so it establishes overlap not sequence, and the two conditions share a trigeminal substrate, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only with the heterogeneity, the bidirectional prevalence, and the inverse papule-pustule finding all carried openly.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: The meta-analysis reports I-squared of 99 percent for prevalence and 98 percent for the pooled odds ratio, and its 95 percent prediction interval of 0.67 to 5.53 includes the null, so the pooled effect does not reliably hold in every population studied; the cross-sectional anchor reports prevalence of each condition within the other, so it establishes overlap rather than temporal sequence; that anchor's inverse association for papules and pustules (OR 0.5) indicates the relationship is phenotype-specific and that subtypes differ, which the authors note requires further stratification; the third anchor is a single-centre 150-patient comparison without subtype or ICHD-3 detail in the abstract; a 2025 Chinese case-control analysis of 200 rosacea patients found no significant association with migraine, an explicit counterweight carried here.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Migraine predating the rosacea diagnosis, unexcludable in designs that condition on either diagnosis
Medication-over-use headache from analgesic or antibiotic use for facial symptoms
Trigeminal neuropeptide pathway shared by both conditions, an alternative explanation in which neither is causal for the other
Concurrent systemic inflammatory or autoimmune disease producing both a facial eruption and headache

evidenceGaps: The meta-analysis reports I-squared of 99 percent for prevalence and 98 percent for the pooled odds ratio, and its 95 percent prediction interval of 0.67 to 5.53 includes the null, so the pooled effect does not reliably hold in every population studied; the cross-sectional anchor reports prevalence of each condition within the other, so it establishes overlap rather than temporal sequence; that anchor's inverse association for papules and pustules (OR 0.5) indicates the relationship is phenotype-specific and that subtypes differ, which the authors note requires further stratification; the third anchor is a single-centre 150-patient comparison without subtype or ICHD-3 detail in the abstract; a 2025 Chinese case-control analysis of 200 rosacea patients found no significant association with migraine, an explicit counterweight carried here.
suggestions.rationale: Authoring registers this edge because the only located synthesis quantifies nearly doubled odds across more than half a million participants, the only clinical-phenotyping anchor identifies which cutaneous features carry the association and which do not, and an independent anchor replicates the direction; the conservative framing carries the meta-analysis' null-spanning prediction interval, the bidirectional prevalence, the inverse papule-pustule finding, the same-publication null, and the shared-trigeminal-substrate alternative, so the overlap is visible while direction remains unasserted.
